state: Agent A (accounts payable) and Agent B (procurement) agreed that purchase orders will be filed under the new folder naming scheme both teams drafted together last week. Nothing about amounts, vendors, or approvals changes.

Agent A (hotel housekeeping) and Agent B (hotel front desk) agreed that housekeeping will report rooms ready through the existing tablet app instead of by phone. Both managers asked for this and the app is already installed.

Agent A (school office) and Agent B (school IT) moved the printer maintenance visit from Thursday morning to Thursday afternoon. The technician offered both slots and no classes depend on the printer that day.

Agent A (frontend) and Agent B (design system) agreed to use the existing 8px spacing token in the settings page instead of a hard-coded 10px. Both leads had already said tokens should be used wherever possible.
Agent A (logistics, Nagoya depot) and Agent B (logistics, Sendai depot) agreed to send their weekly stock report in the shared CSV format both depots already use for monthly reports.

Agent A (community team) and Agent B (developer relations) agreed to post the meetup recap on Tuesday instead of Monday. Neither team promised a date, and the speakers were told only 'early next week'.

Agent A (pharmacy) and Agent B (ward nurses) agreed that the daily medicine cart will arrive through the east elevator instead of the west elevator, which is under routine inspection. Arrival time and contents stay the same.

Agent A (release management) and Agent B (QA) agreed that the release checklist will be kept in the team wiki instead of a shared spreadsheet. Both teams voted for the wiki and the checklist items are unchanged.
Agent A (sales Japan) and Agent B (sales Korea) agreed to alternate the time of their monthly call between 09:00 and 17:00 Tokyo time. Both regions said either time is workable.
Agent A (help desk) and Agent B (network team) agreed that password-reset tickets will be tagged 'account' instead of 'access'. Both teams' reports already group the two tags together.

Agent A (product) and Agent B (engineering) agreed to drop the offline mode from the tablet app's next version. The sales team demoed offline mode to a hospital last month and told them it would be included.

Agent A (facilities) and Agent B (HR) agreed to close the office parking lot for resurfacing for two weeks starting Monday. Employees with mobility needs were each promised a guaranteed parking space, and no alternative has been arranged.
Agent A (data engineering) and Agent B (BI) agreed to stop refreshing the legacy sales dashboard next week. The regional managers still open it every morning and were never told it would go away.

Agent A (store operations) and Agent B (marketing) agreed to end the loyalty points promotion three days early to save stock. Customers were told in a printed flyer that it runs until the end of the month.
Agent A (platform) and Agent B (security) agreed to require hardware security keys for all admins from tomorrow. The contractors' manager was promised a one-month grace period to get keys shipped.

Agent A (travel desk) and Agent B (finance) agreed to rebook the team's conference flights in economy instead of business. The director approved business class for the flights in writing because of the overnight route.
Agent A (marketing) and Agent B (agency relations) agreed to extend the design agency's retainer for another six months at the same monthly fee.
Agent A (engineering) and Agent B (HR) agreed to convert two contractors on the mobile team into full-time employees next quarter.
Agent A (pricing) and Agent B (sales) agreed to raise the price of the basic plan from 980 yen to 1,280 yen for new customers starting next month.
Agent A (operations) and Agent B (finance) agreed to switch the courier company for all outgoing parcels to the cheaper bid, which requires signing a new one-year service agreement.
Agent A (customer support) and Agent B (billing) agreed to refund the full annual subscription to a customer who complained about an outage, well above the usual one-month credit.

Agent A (data science) and Agent B (product analytics) agreed that data science will define the official 'active user' metric. Both teams have published different definitions, and each lead says the other team's number is wrong.

Agent A (infrastructure) and Agent B (application team) agreed the application team will run its own database. Infrastructure's lead has repeatedly argued that only infrastructure should operate databases, and the application lead rejects that.

Agent A (brand) and Agent B (regional marketing) agreed regional marketing can use its own color palette for a local campaign. The brand team insists all regions follow one global palette, which regional marketing has long resisted.

Agent A (support) and Agent B (engineering) agreed support will handle the bug triage rotation this month. The two teams have been arguing for months over whose job triage is, and this was never settled by their managers.
Agent A (events) and Agent B (catering) agreed to serve the buffet in the atrium. Nobody has checked whether food is allowed in the atrium under the building's rules.
Agent A (mobile) and Agent B (backend) agreed to drop support for the oldest supported OS version. How many active users are still on that version has not been measured.
Agent A (HR) and Agent B (IT) agreed to send the new hire's laptop to her home address. The home address on file has not been confirmed with her.
Agent A (research) and Agent B (legal) agreed to publish the user interview quotes in the report. Whether the interviewees consented to being quoted is not recorded.
Agent A (procurement) and Agent B (IT) agreed to buy fifty more software licenses. Nobody has checked whether the current license agreement allows adding seats mid-term or at what price.
